text:
maya: quick question — I'm bringing up a new external model 'kestrel-6.5b' into our onboarding flow. The repo includes a license called 'NonCommercial-Attribution v1.0' (attached). Can we: 1) quantize it and include the quantized weights in Dedicated images or ship to on-prem customers? 2) run our eval suite and publish benchmark numbers on our public benchmarks page? 3) add it to the model-registry with a 'preview' flag so internal teams can test?

owen: short answers upfront: probably not for 1 and 2 without further review. NC (non-commercial) + attribution usually prohibits commercial hosting/redistribution. A few clarifications: hosting the model behind a paid API (hosted or Dedicated paid pools) == commercial use. Shipping derivative weights to customers == redistribution of a derivative, also commercial if customers pay. Internal evals for due diligence are typically OK, but publishing public benchmarks could trigger redistribution/derivative concerns if license has sharealike or publicity clauses. Need full license text to confirm.

leah: infra take — quantized weights we produce are derivatives; packaging them into a docker image and delivering to a customer is redistribution. So from an ops perspective, if license forbids redistribution/commercial use, we must block shipping quantized weights. We can still run evaluation runners against the original upstream checkpoint if the repo allows download, or ask customers to BYO.

sam: product question — is BYO (bring-your-own) model the right fallback? i.e., let customers upload their own kestrel-6.5b to their Private/Dedicated instance and we supply the inference runtime and prompts/recipes. Also what wording should we use for attribution if the license requires it?

owen: BYO is the safest commercial path. Guidance checklist (legal):
- get the full license text and any contributor/third-party exceptions
- confirm whether "NonCommercial" is defined (some NC clauses allow research partners)
- determine whether attribution clause requires specific text/placement (UI, docs, or model outputs)
- check for "no derivative" or "share-alike" language — that affects quantization and redistribution
- if redistribution prohibited, BYO or linking to upstream checkpoint is the path

Suggested minimal attribution to display in UI/docs if allowed: "Model: Kestrel-6.5B — Copyright (c) 2024 KestrelAI. Licensed under NonCommercial-Attribution v1.0. Use subject to license: <license_url>"

Also suggested model-registry metadata fields we need to capture (for ops + legal):
```
model_name: "kestrel-6.5b"
upstream_url: "https://github.com/kestrelai/kestrel-6.5b"
license_name: "NonCommercial-Attribution v1.0"
license_url: "https://github.com/kestrelai/kestrel-6.5b/LICENSE"
commercial_use_allowed: "no"
redistribution_allowed: "no"
modification_allowed: "?"  # depends on license text
attribution_required: "yes"
provenance_notes: "upstream checkpoint, date, commit"
```

leah: ops note — we'll add a hard flag in the registry UI that prevents creating Dedicated images or export packages if `redistribution_allowed` == "no". That should prevent accidental shipping.

license-bot: automated scan result: license contains NC + ATTR clauses. Flags: commercial_use:false, redistribution:false, attribution:required. Confidence: medium. Link to parsed license: https://legal.redwood/checks/1719909999

maya: thanks all — I'll attach the LICENSE + README to this thread and open a model-registry PR marking it restricted. Plan: run internal evals only and set public benchmarks to "hold" until legal confirms. I'll also add a BYO doc for sales.

owen: legal will review the full license doc. If there are any downstream exceptions or a dual-license option, we can reassess. For now, treat as restricted (no hosting/redistribution). I'll add required attribution text in the PR review comments.

sam: noted. I'll update the sales FAQ to recommend BYO and to avoid promising hosted availability.

Action items:
- maya: attach license + open model-registry PR (blocked -> restricted).
- owen: legal review and confirmation (deadline: 48h).
- leah: add guard in registry UI to block image builds for restricted models.
- sam: update sales docs / BYO guidance.
